newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA SNATCH VICTORY WITH LATE GOAL.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA SNATCH VICTORY WITH LATE GOAL.

text.p: Russia kept alive their hopes of reaching the final stages of the world ice hockey championship with a late goal by Alexander Barkov for a 5-4 win against France on Wednesday.
Showing superior skating and individual puck handling skills in the first half of the pool A match, Russia seemed headed for an easy victory.
Alexei Chupin, Anatoly Fedotov, Dmitry Krasotkin and Alexander Prokopiev scored a goal each and Russia led 4-0 after 23 minutes.
But France refused to cave in and their team spirit soared as Roger Dube and Pierre Allard, assisted by Dube, scored two goals inside 74 seconds halway into the second period.
Six minutes later, Dube found the net again to leave France just one goal behind.

The French comeback mercilessly highlighted the chief weaknesses of the Russian side - the lack of a reliable goalkeeper, and nonexistent teamwork when the going gets tough. Sergei Fadeyev in the Russian goal made many mistakes.

Four minutes before the end, Arnaud Briand equalised and for a brief moment France looked capable of snatching a draw - a dropped point could have undermined Russia's chances to reach the final series.
But the individual brilliance of centre forward Barkov salavaged the game for Russia just 21 seconds after the equaliser.
With French still euphoric after equalising, Barkov outsmarted their defence, coolly waited out French goaltender Francois Gravel and whipped the puck into the net.
Russia have five points from three games but have yet to play 1996 world champions the Czech Republic and 1995 world champions Finland.
France, with three straight losses, are certain to travel to Tampere for the relegation play-offs after the preliminary round-robin groups.
